items.q: What should you remember about **Task switching ≠ cognitive flexibility**?
items.a: **flexibility is broader; switching requires** flexibility but adds the start/stop cost of changing operational mode.

items.q: What should you remember about **Unfair self-expectation**?
items.a: **immediate deep focus on boring/new material is biologically** unrealistic; texting a awaited message is instant because salience is high, not because attention is broken.

items.q: What should you remember about **Push-pull neural circuits**?
items.a: **switching = ramp some** networks up, dim others down; takes minutes, not milliseconds.

items.q: What should you remember about **Arbitrary transition labels work**?
items.a: **top-down designation ("this is transition")** improves next-task performance even at 15 s; count 10→1 or 1→10.

items.q: What should you remember about **Phone between tasks is task C**?
items.a: **new context, images, and** ideas intrude; worst common transition mistake.

items.q: What should you remember about **Limit environmental grab-attention**?
items.a: **walk past World Cup crowd** on lab monitors without joining; scruff yourself toward task B.

items.q: What should you remember about **Three critical tasks/day**?
items.a: **write 1–3 (never more) cognitively** demanding goals; everything else is automaticity; exercise/social life not on the list.

items.q: What should you remember about **Visual time-domain drill**?
items.a: **eyes closed (interoception) → hand surface → ~10 ft → ~50 ft** → horizon → close eyes return; ~5–15 s per station; trains the same near/far time-slicing shift required when changing tasks; Huberman does daily ~2 min.
